parts.text: Mr. Josue had a certain amount of capital to fund his store.
He received $4000 from the first bank and twice that amount from the second bank.
After receiving the loans, his total capital became $17000.
How much capital did Mr. Josue initially have before receiving the loans?

parts.text: Mr. Josue sought financial assistance from two banks to support his shop.
He received $4000 from the first bank, while the second bank provided him with double that amount.
Given that he initially had a capital of $5000, what is his current capital?

parts.text: Mr. Josue is an entrepreneur who decided to expand his store.
To fund this expansion, he solicited money from two banks.
The first bank, Bank A, gave him $4000.
At the same time, he also received a loan from Bank B, which was twice as much as what he got from Bank A.
However, Bank B also offered him an additional $3000 as a business development grant, which he decided not to accept.
Before soliciting funds from the banks, Mr. Josue initially had $5000 in capital.
Considering all these transactions, how much capital does Mr. Josue have now for his store expansion?

parts.text: Lillian's garden doesn't have any bird feeders in it so she wants to add some.
She builds 5 and purchases 2 others.

Each bird feeder seems to attract 30 birds throughout the day until Lillian noticed that the birds seem to prefer the feeders she made herself which attract 15 more birds each than the store-bought ones.
How many birds can Lillian expect to see in her garden each day if the same amount keep coming to her bird feeders?
